how: Line 2290: `!!p` is reached only when !n and !same(p,n) (the same(p,n) block at line 2282 returns first), so !n implies p non-null; the operand is always true.

Line 2298: `p.id !== n.id` for a non-armed n is already rejected by the identity guard at line 2285 (p && n && id differs && n.phase !== armed), which runs before ok; the armed branch returns earlier. The operand never sees an id mismatch.

Line 2299: n captured with action auto.captureOutgoing needs p armed by the guard at line 2248 (capture with p?.phase !== armed fails first), so `p.phase === armed` is implied by the neighbouring `action.t === auto.captureOutgoing` operand.

Line 1104: a Keep's succeededAtStep and succeededAtMs are written together (moves.ts line 207; line 951 and the step invariant at line 2496 reject a half-written pair), so succeededAtStep === null iff succeededAtMs === null and the neighbouring operand skips the same records.
Line 1104: same pairing fact as #1 (moves.ts line 207, invariants line 951 and 2496): succeededAtMs === null iff succeededAtStep === null, so the first operand already skips every such record.

After a purge, line 1113 sets the end step (state purged after the Keep) and line 1117 (w.step >= endStep) skips the inbox, so the clause `fi.closingSinceMs === null` (and the other closing-time guards) cannot change a verdict; purge (fakeflux.ts:100) keeps the delete cause and both closing times, so only 1113/1117 exclude it.
line 1119: flux-caused closings are already skipped by endStep (line 1112) and the w.step >= endStep test (line 1117), so the delete-cause test cannot change a verdict.
